Node2Shell exploitation, Magento PolyShell and Volt Typhoon 'Silent Train' continue, with no change in actions. No new major cloud or developer platform breaches surfaced since the 16:50 UTC update. headline: Update Chrome to 156: Anthropic says an unreleased Claude model found and fully exploited critical Chrome flaws, and Google fixed 62 of them. PHP2Shell is being used in real, AI-assisted intrusions: a China-linked actor using Claude Code and DeepSeek/Kimi tooling chained it with a Linux kernel flaw to root 25 servers, mostly firewalls, and tunnel into a US government-affiliated network (patch PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, update the kernel and get firewall vendor fixes); CISA confirms the Brotli 'Node2Shell' flaw is exploited (Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1), and Magento PolyShell has breached hundreds of stores. Still act on: Comet's Opik leak of AI provider keys, CyberStrikeAI's 44-agent campaign, n0n's AI-built extortion kit, ConnectWise (Storm-0940 with ARTEX), Cathedral's agent intrusion into Anthropic, Warp, the testmetest npm worm and Railway secrets. Volt Typhoon's newly exposed 'Silent Train' relay network used edge-management zero-days, so lock down admin interfaces.
ai_headline: AI is now both finding and weaponizing flaws: Anthropic's red team showed a Claude model building a one-click Chrome sandbox escape (62 Chrome CVEs patched), and the first documented real intrusion with AI-found PHP2Shell was itself AI-assisted (Claude Code, DeepSeek and Kimi on the attacker's servers, 25 servers rooted). Criminals and states run AI agents at scale (CyberStrikeAI's 44 agents, Storm-0940's ARTEX at ConnectWise, n0n's opencode agent), AI coding tools are delivery routes and loot (testmetest, Aokigahara, fake GPT-6 and Claude installers), and AI keys and ML servers remain targets (Railway, treg, Comet Opik, OpenCode, LiteLLM, MLflow).

focus.title: Anthropic: an unreleased Claude research model found and fully exploited critical flaws in Chrome and other major software; Chrome 156 fixes 62 of them
focus.vendor: Google Chrome (plus other browsers and operating systems)
focus.why: New (Oct 27): Anthropic's Frontier Red Team says an internal, unreleased Claude model found critical bugs and wrote five complete attack chains with little or no user interaction, including a one-click Chrome exploit that chains a V8 heap bug, a V8 sandbox and ASLR bypass, a CacheStorage race and a FedCM use-after-free to run code outside Chrome's sandbox on default macOS Chrome. Google assigned and patched 62 critical or high CVEs from this work in Chrome 156 (13 sandbox escapes); Chrome 156's release notes also credit OpenAI Codex Security for a Turbolev use-after-free. Other chains are under 90-day coordinated disclosure, so their vendors' fixes may not be public yet. No attacks using these bugs are reported.
focus.action: Update Chrome to 156.0.8078.73/.74 (Windows, Mac) or 156.0.8078.73 (Linux, Android) and restart the browser; update Chromium-based browsers such as Edge as their builds ship. Keep OS and browser auto-updates on, since the other chains' fixes may land quietly.
focus.ai_note: AI as the cause: the model both found the flaws and built working multi-step exploits; expect the same capability in attackers' hands soon.

focus.title: TrendAI: CyberStrikeAI platform ran 44 AI agents to attack at least 19 organizations, mostly in Japan; more AI-run campaigns documented
focus.vendor: Multiple (edge devices, VPNs, WebLogic, AI endpoints)
focus.why: New (Oct 27): Trend Micro's TrendAI analysed three exposed attacker servers. In one, the open-source CyberStrikeAI tool split an attack across 44 AI agents (recon, finding and validating flaws, exploitation, command and control, persistence, data theft and reporting) and wrote Japanese-language fake login pages; at least 19 organizations, 16 in Japan, were hit with validation activity in a short October burst, and the same operator also targeted Taiwan and Hong Kong. A second, human-led but LLM-assisted campaign (24 days, Aug-Sep) targeted AI workflow platforms and inference services to get cheap inference, and stole cadastral records, Windows credentials and email from a GIS server left on default credentials. A third operator used AI to write tools for at least six campaigns (Jan-Oct) against Cisco, Citrix, F5 and Yamaha edge devices and WebLogic servers, using published flaws and credentials in config files. The Hacker News round-up also lists Unit 42 cases: actor 'BUGSTER' ran the Hermes agent framework on DeepSeek V4 with Cursor (safety controls off) against Indian universities (one database of 5,200+ student records taken), and a human operator used frontier models to breach an enterprise network largely autonomously in 10 hours, pull hard-coded tokens from code repos and turn the victim's AI endpoints into attack infrastructure; plus a Gentlemen ransomware affiliate using Claude Code in six intrusions (late June), the Zerofot 'auto_scan' tool that used OpenAI Codex and Claude Code to harvest thousands of API keys from exposed hosts, and an AI-generated 'RAGE' framework hitting Redis, Elasticsearch, Docker, Jenkins and similar services. TrendAI found no evidence the three server cases share an operator.
focus.action: Patch internet-facing VPN and edge devices (Cisco, Citrix, F5, Yamaha) and WebLogic, remove default credentials (especially on GIS and admin consoles) and strip credentials from device config files. Keep Redis, Elasticsearch, Docker, Jenkins, Hadoop YARN and AI inference endpoints off the internet or behind authentication, set spending limits on AI provider keys and watch for unexplained inference usage. Scan code repositories for hard-coded tokens and rotate any found.
focus.ai_note: AI as the cause: in the CyberStrikeAI case AI agents ran the whole attack workflow; in the others AI assisted planning, tool-writing or ran large parts of the intrusion. Which models were used is mostly not known.

focus.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain breach run by China-linked Storm-0940 using ARTEX AI agents
focus.why: Microsoft says Storm-0940 took over the identities of several ConnectWise Cloud Backup cloud apps on Oct 15 and used them, via the ARTEX agentic AI pentest framework, to sign in to customer Microsoft 365 tenants that had already granted those apps access, then ran reconnaissance, added app credentials and changed privileged roles. Some victims went from first targeting to privileged access in under 3 hours, and app credentials the attackers added can keep working after the original app is fixed. Wiz (Oct 23) sees the same actor probing other software vendors' SSO and Okta/Entra sign-ins. ConnectWise is restoring services in phases and has notified the UK ICO; The Telegraph (Oct 24) reports the UK NCSC is working with Microsoft to find out whether British organisations were compromised. Huntress (Oct 26) says its own telemetry is consistent with Microsoft's finding and looks like an AI agent driving scripted tools with occasional human input.
focus.action: If you use ConnectWise Cloud Backup (or any MSP with app access to your tenant): in Entra ID review the ConnectWise enterprise apps and every app or service principal for credentials, owners or role assignments added since Oct 15 and remove what you did not add; review Graph and directory audit logs and sign-ins from 144.172.64[.]99; follow ConnectWise's and Microsoft's guidance. Make sure password-spray protections and MFA cover Entra and Okta accounts.
focus.ai_note: AI ran the attack: Microsoft says the ARTEX AI agents did the password spraying, OAuth app abuse and follow-on directory changes 'at machine speed' (up to 2,900 sign-in attempts per minute across 2,250+ tenants).

focus.title: Cathedral's AI agents got into Anthropic's sales, HR and IT systems through third-party business software in under 12 hours
focus.vendor: Anthropic / unnamed third-party sales and admin SaaS
focus.why: New (Washington Post, Oct 26): security startup Cathedral, testing under Anthropic's outside-researcher program, says its autonomous AI agents found paths into Anthropic's internal business systems in less than 12 hours by exploiting flaws in third-party administrative and sales software that many other companies also use, after days of failing to break Anthropic's own software. Its draft report says the agents could reach meeting transcripts, salary and offer details and Slack messages about advanced models. Anthropic confirms access to a limited set of sales, HR and IT systems holding customer and partner business contacts and basic user account records, says Claude conversations, source code and model weights were not touched, cut access the same day and disabled the software until vendors shipped fixes. Anthropic says Cathedral did not disclose all its activity and overstated the risk; it found no sign anyone else used the flaws. The vendors and flaws are not named.
focus.action: Nothing to patch yet because the vendors are unnamed. Treat it as a warning that AI agents go after the SaaS around you: review which third-party sales, HR and IT apps hold sensitive data, cut their access scopes and admin accounts, and turn on alerting for unusual API and admin activity in them. If you are an Anthropic business customer, expect phishing that uses your business contact details.
focus.ai_note: AI as the cause: autonomous agents found the way in; also an AI-provider breach, though no model data or customer prompts were reached.

focus.title: Warp says an AI 'agent swarm' broke in through a vendor and read agent trace and telemetry data of up to ~1% of users
focus.why: New (Warp CEO Zach Lloyd, Oct 26; BleepingComputer, Oct 27): on Oct 23 Warp found an active, narrow exploitation of a third-party vendor in its infrastructure. Lloyd says the attack appears to have come from an agent swarm using a sophisticated penetration and escalation technique, likely starting with a hole in a vendor dependency, and it reached a limited amount of agent trace and telemetry data for at most about 1% of users. Warp says it detected and remediated it within hours, notified users it identified as affected, and is investigating with CrowdStrike and law enforcement. The vendor, the flaw and whether secrets that appeared in agent traces were exposed have not been disclosed. It is the second AI-agent intrusion via third-party software this week after Cathedral's access to Anthropic.
focus.action: If you use Warp, watch for a notice from Warp and follow its instructions. If your Warp agent sessions ever printed or handled secrets (API keys, tokens, .env values, cloud credentials), rotate them, since agent traces can contain command output. Nothing to update on your side yet.
focus.ai_note: Warp attributes the intrusion to an AI agent swarm (not independently confirmed), and the stolen data is AI coding-agent traces.

focus.title: n0n extortion group used an AI coding agent to build its attack toolkit; 93 victims listed, $283.7M demanded
focus.vendor: Multiple (FortiGate SSL-VPN, RDP/WinRM, AWS keys, hosting portals, Cisco FMC)
focus.why: New (Oct 28): SOCRadar found an exposed staging server (185.157.161[.]148:8877) holding a n0n operator's September workspace: 829 scripts, locker source code and extortion infrastructure. The operator used the open-source opencode AI coding agent, configured with 154 model entries across seven providers (including 'uncensored'/'abliterated' models and a self-hosted one), to write and debug hundreds of attack scripts, spending more than $7,216 on LLM usage. Entry was by credentials only, not software flaws: credential stuffing against 305 FortiGate SSL-VPN devices, exposed AWS keys, weak RDP/WinRM logins and reused hosting-portal sessions. The operator hijacked Cisco Firepower Management Center to switch access policies to BLOCK, and sometimes deleted data and backups instead of encrypting. As of Oct 19 n0n listed 93 victims and $283.7M in total demands; SOCRadar says the operation is human-directed with AI support, not autonomous.
focus.action: Require MFA on SSL-VPN, RDP/WinRM and hosting/admin portals, block credential stuffing (rate limits, lockouts, geo or residential-proxy blocking), rotate and remove long-lived AWS access keys, check for hidden admin accounts disguised as services, lock down firewall management consoles, keep offline or immutable backups, and block 185.157.161.148.
focus.ai_note: AI as the cause: an AI coding agent wrote the group's tooling, letting a small crew run a broad credential-driven extortion campaign.

focus.title: PHP2Shell: unauthenticated RCE in the PHP runtime, exploited (CISA KEV); AI-assisted China-linked actor rooted 25 servers, mostly firewalls, and reached a US government-affiliated network
focus.why: New (Oct 28, The Hacker News on Dream's report): the intrusion was AI-assisted. Dream found Anthropic's Claude Code installed on the attack infrastructure, API keys for FOFA and for an AI offensive platform called aiscan configured with DeepSeek and Kimi models, and nearly 40 scripts whose structure suggests AI-written code. The exploit is a custom, non-public build tailored to one large vendor's firewall OS, which runs PHP 8.0.30 on its appweb management server. Of 240 filtered targets, 24 were rooted in an automated batch and a 25th, an internal firewall management server, through a reverse SSH tunnel; 22 rooted firewalls still hold web shells and the tunnel into the US government-affiliated network is likely still running. Whether the Active Directory password spraying or backdoor accounts succeeded is unknown. Separately, forum members quoted by Flare say turning the public PoC into reliable attacks is hard, which fits the limited exploitation seen so far. New (Oct 28): Dream reports (via SecurityWeek) that a China-linked actor used FOFA to find 19,000 internet-facing firewalls from one vendor, narrowed them to 240 in the US, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea running newer PHP, and on Oct 23-24 used an automated tool to chain PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw (CVE-2026-46300), dropping a root PHP web shell on 24 devices. At one US government-affiliated organization the attacker tunnelled in over reverse SSH, hit the internal firewall management server with the same chain, took the configs and credentials of every managed firewall, decrypted the LDAP service-account password, password-sprayed and tried to create AD backdoor accounts. Delft's tracker now counts 72,343 exploitation requests from 659 IPs (174 sending code or droppers). Axios notes millions of attempts have produced few confirmed compromises so far. New (Oct 28): Praetorian's analysis calls PHP2Shell exploitable but conditional and hard to mass-exploit, which matches CrowdStrike and Wiz; patch anyway, since exploitation against web servers and Palo Alto management interfaces is confirmed. New (Oct 27, afternoon): Palo Alto Networks raised its advisory to Critical / highest urgency and now says active exploitation has been observed against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet (the affected part is the management web UI and XML API, and data-plane interfaces with a management profile; GlobalProtect and Captive Portal are not affected). New hotfixes released today: 12.2.4-h1, 12.1.7-h11, 10.2.13-h27 and 10.2.16-h12; 11.2.13-h4 is due Oct 27, 11.2.16-h1 Oct 28, 12.1.4-h13, 11.2.7-h23 and 10.2.10-h42 Oct 29, and 12.1.10-h3, 11.2.4-h23, 11.1.7-h12 and 10.2.7-h39 Oct 30. New (Oct 26): CISA added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and updated its alert, telling organizations to patch to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 and to take unpatched or end-of-life (8.1 and older) PHP systems offline; posts on X say US agencies have until Oct 29. Palo Alto Networks also published an impact advisory for its products. Earlier: successful exploitation is confirmed, and appliance vendors are now listing affected products (Cisco advisory; Siemens, Schneider Electric and ABB for some industrial products, per SecurityWeek). Perplexity's Adel Karimi recorded 35 shells spawned by Apache workers on three PHP 8.4.26 mod_php honeypots on Oct 24, from 15.204.59.70 (OVH US) and 162.35.99.94 (Interserver), using the public exploit's offsets; Expel's Marcus Hutchins called it the highest-quality confirmation so far (BleepingComputer). Delft Threat Intelligence Lab's live tracker counts 42,034 exploitation requests from 597 IPs since Oct 21, 171 of them sending code or droppers, and Trail of Bits reportedly has a production-grade root exploit for mod_php and php-fpm. No second-stage payload download was seen on the honeypots, and as of Oct 26 morning CISA had still not added the flaws to KEV (SecurityWeek). How many real servers are compromised is unknown. Two flaws in the PHP engine (CVSS 9.8 in NVD, 9.2 CVSS v4) allow unauthenticated remote code execution via crafted HTTP requests, so WordPress, Drupal and Joomla sites are exposed even with clean app code. Correction: on Oct 25 Unit 42 retracted its Oct 23 update that tied an AI-agent intrusion at a European government agency to PHP2Shell; it still saw the attack inside a vulnerable PHP application but cannot confirm PHP2Shell was the way in. Its brief still urges immediate patching, and Cortex Xpanse counts 22.6 million potentially exposed instances. Amazon says PHP2Shell 'is now seeing broad exploitation attempts in the wild' (first attempt Oct 17, before the patch) but cannot say whether any would have succeeded; TechCrunch (Oct 24) reported Palo Alto Networks and Trail of Bits had confirmed compromises (Palo Alto's part may rest on the retracted Unit 42 update), and researchers report working code execution on PHP 8.2 and 8.3 too (no universal exploit); Cloudflare saw millions of attempts and Sophos and Arctic Wolf report Mirai install attempts. The PHP Foundation and Dataminr still report no confirmed compromises of their own and CrowdStrike says weaponising obstacles likely limit mass exploitation, but FBI (Oct 23 PSA) and CISA urge immediate patching. A separate RCE path (CVE-2026-115560) in unusual session configurations is not fixed by the Oct 21 releases. Palo Alto PAN-OS and Panorama management interfaces (web UI and XML API) are affected; as of Oct 26 hotfixes are out for 10.2.18-h13, 11.1.4-h38, 11.1.6-h40, 11.1.10-h36, 11.1.13-h16, 11.1.16-h4 and 11.2.10-h16, the rest are due Oct 27-30, Palo Alto knows of no exploitation against its products and says CVE-2026-115560 does not affect PAN-OS (WF-500 is now listed as not affected); Cisco has an advisory too. TechCrunch (Oct 24) reports a large number of systems remain unpatched. Google Cloud's advisory (updated Oct 23 with Mandiant guidance) warns that upgrading PHP packages on disk leaves the vulnerable code loaded in running php-fpm, Apache, FrankenPHP or LiteSpeed workers until they are restarted, and that edge, gateway and management appliances often embed PHP. Update (Oct 27): BleepingComputer and The Hacker News report CISA has confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. New (Oct 27): CISA gave US federal agencies until Oct 29 to patch (TechCrunch). Wiz says the number of internet-exposed vulnerable machines it sees fell about 67% since disclosure, that the attempts in its own telemetry have not succeeded so far and that it has not seen a public end-to-end exploit, though partners have privately shared working ones. New (Oct 28): the Delft Threat Intelligence Lab's honeypots logged 72,515 PHP2Shell exploit requests from 664 IPs since Oct 21, with 175 IPs sending code or a dropper.
focus.action: If you run firewalls or appliances with internet-facing management interfaces, take those interfaces off the internet now and ask your vendor whether its embedded PHP (including PHP 8.0.x) is patched against PHP2Shell, since the attacker fingerprinted about 19,000 such devices. Also patch the Linux kernel for Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300) on appliances and servers running PHP, and if an internet-facing firewall or appliance ran vulnerable PHP, check it for PHP web shells and reverse SSH tunnels and rotate the credentials stored on it and its management server (including LDAP service accounts). Upgrade to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 (check the runtime serving web traffic, including containers), then explicitly restart php-fpm, apache2/httpd, frankenphp or lsws and any supervisor-managed workers; on a host that shows signs of probing (for example oversized PHPSESSID cookies), capture worker memory first, since a restart destroys the evidence. Use official distro security repositories rather than lagging third-party mirrors, and inventory appliances that embed PHP and apply Cisco, Siemens, Schneider Electric and ABB fixes as they ship. 8.1 and older get no official release, so use a vendor-patched package or move to a supported branch. Also set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until PHP's next routine release (blocks CVE-2026-115560). If you can't patch now, take internet-facing PHP systems offline (FBI/CISA advice; a WAF is only a stopgap). Search logs for 15.204.59.70 and 162.35.99.94, and hunt back to Oct 17 for PHP workers launching shells or downloading files (CISA's SIGMA rule and Unit 42's XQL queries help); if found, treat the host's credentials (including AD and MFA secrets) as stolen and report compromises to IC3. Palo Alto: restrict management web UI and XML API to trusted IPs, remove management profiles from untrusted interfaces, enable Threat IDs 543004 and 97622-97625, and install the PAN-OS hotfix for your branch now that exploitation is confirmed (12.2.4-h1, 12.1.7-h11, 11.1.x and 10.2.13/16/18 hotfixes are out; the rest are due Oct 27-30 per Palo Alto's advisory); if your management interface was internet-facing, check it for compromise.
focus.ai_note: AI found it and AI helped exploit it: Calif, Wiz (Atlas agent) and OpenAI's Codex Security found the bugs with AI help, and Dream's evidence (Claude Code, aiscan with DeepSeek and Kimi, AI-styled scripts) makes the firewall campaign the first documented AI-assisted real intrusion using PHP2Shell. Unit 42's earlier AI-agent PHP2Shell claim remains retracted.

focus.title: Brotli decoder RCE ('Node2Shell', 'Broccoli2Shell'): in CISA KEV and public exploit now seen in the wild; Node.js, Bun, .NET, Envoy, Python
focus.why: New (Oct 28): BleepingComputer and SecurityWeek report CISA's confirmation of Node2Shell exploitation; US federal agencies must patch by Nov 10, and CISA advises blocking incoming Brotli-compressed requests or disabling Brotli decoding until patched, then restarting processes and rebuilding container images. New (Oct 28): ELLIO says its sensors recorded the public Node2Shell exploit (aimed at Node v24.22.0) in the wild from 94.154.43.7, an IP also exploiting PHP2Shell, which it reads as a mass-exploitation operator; Previdian logged one attempt on its honeypots. Wiz says 91% of cloud environments have vulnerable resources and 82% expose Node.js publicly, while Sysdig notes real exposure depends on decoding attacker-supplied Brotli (Express 5 with default JSON parsing qualifies). Palo Alto (updated Oct 28) says PAN-OS is only exposed when Brotli inspection with TLS decryption is on (check 'show system setting brotli'); hotfixes 12.2.4-h1, 12.1.7-h11, 11.2.7-h23, 11.2.10-h17, 11.2.13-h4 and 11.2.16-h1 are out, with 12.1.4-h13 due Oct 29 and 12.1.10-h3 and 11.2.4-h23 due Oct 30; it is not aware of exploitation against its products. New (Oct 27): CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, meaning it has evidence of exploitation in the wild (US federal deadline Nov 10); details of the attacks have not been published. Palo Alto says one PAN-OS hotfix covers both PHP2Shell and Brotli, except 11.2.10-h16 (PHP only; use 11.2.10-h17). New (Oct 26): PHP rebuilt its official Windows packages for 8.2-8.5 because last week's builds bundled vulnerable Brotli 1.2.0, reachable through the cURL extension when automatic decompression is on (CURLOPT_ENCODING), which the Guzzle HTTP library sets by default, so a malicious server a PHP app contacts could send a crafted response (The Hacker News). Palo Alto Networks published a portfolio status advisory for the flaw. Earlier today Microsoft released out-of-band .NET updates (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14, .NET 11 RC3); public proof-of-concept exploits are on GitHub, and CISA now lists it as exploited. An out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder (versions 1.0.3-1.2.0, CVSS v4 9.2) lets crafted compressed data from an unauthenticated attacker corrupt memory and possibly run code, on servers that decode Brotli request bodies (e.g. Express 5 body parsers) and on clients that fetch Brotli responses (Node.js fetch()). Imperva demonstrated working code execution on the official Node.js 24.22.0 arm64 build, and The Hacker News (Oct 24) confirms Bun, the Python brotli and brotlicffi packages and Envoy proxies that decompress Brotli are affected. ELLIO (Oct 25) reproduced code execution on official x86-64 Node.js 24.22.0 builds (plain node:http, the node:24.22.0-slim image, Express 5.3.0 and Koa 3), says failed attempts crash workers and can leave other users' credentials in core dumps, and saw a public 'node2shell-check' scanner already mapping which hosts decompress Brotli. Before CISA's listing no in-the-wild exploitation had been reported. Note process.versions.brotli shows 1.2.0 on patched and unpatched Node builds, so check the Node release version.
focus.action: Update .NET to 8.0.33, 9.0.22 or 10.0.14 (apps that decode Brotli), Node.js to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 (20.x and older get no fix), Bun to 1.4.4+, PHP on Windows to the rebuilt 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 or 8.2.35-1 packages (php -v won't change; check the -1 file name or the SHA-256), the Brotli library to 1.0.10, 1.1.1 or 1.2.1, and Envoy and Python Brotli packages per their advisories; rebuild container images that bundle a Node binary. On PAN-OS, use the PHP2Shell hotfix for your branch (11.2.10-h17, not -h16), or until then disable Brotli inspection with 'set system setting brotli-encoding disable'; update Prisma Cloud Application Security Transporter Client to 0.2.9. Also update Ruby brotli gem (0.9.1/0.9.2), distro libbrotli packages and anything built with bun build --compile. Until patched, drop inbound Content-Encoding: br where you can. Go programs using the andybalholm/brotli port (pulled in by fasthttp and Fiber) should move to v1.2.7, per an X post (unverified).
focus.ai_note: Disputed AI discovery: OpenAI said on X (Oct 23) that it found the bug during an AI red-teaming exercise, but BleepingComputer (Oct 26) credits Imperva's Red Team with finding it. The root cause had been fixed in Brotli's source in February without being recognised as a security flaw.

focus.title: Railway platform breach: ~100,000 workspaces' secrets possibly decrypted, attacker hunting AI keys
focus.why: Railway's preliminary report (published today) says the attack ran from Oct 20 13:58 to Oct 22 03:32 UTC: the attacker escalated privileges via build infrastructure, reached CI credentials and decrypted a subset of customer environment variables, up to 1.85% of workspaces (about 100,000). Railway says the attacker wanted AI and platform API keys for model distillation and targeted workspaces with many env vars or many AI keys. It asked GitHub, GitLab, Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Stripe and others to revoke keys, so a revocation email does not by itself mean your key was stolen. Users on X report unauthorised usage of their Anthropic and OpenAI keys (unverified individual reports). Source-code access is not yet ruled out. Separately, Swell's swETH and rswETH oracle hot keys were compromised on Oct 21 and used to inflate token rates; a researcher suggested a Railway link, but it is a timing correlation only (unconfirmed). Railway's Oct 24 status note says it is not under a new attack: OpenAI and Anthropic revoked another batch of keys as a precaution, and because Railway could not filter by date, some replacement keys created after the incident were revoked too.
focus.action: Anyone who stored secrets on Railway before Oct 21: rotate every env var and revoke old keys at the issuing provider (AI keys first, then database, registry, cloud, Stripe and GitHub tokens), create new Railway API/project tokens, reconnect GitHub and redeploy bucket services, remove public network access to databases, and check provider usage, GitHub and registry audit logs back to Oct 20. If a provider revoked a replacement key, create a new one, update the Railway variable and redeploy; this does not mean the replacement was compromised.
focus.ai_note: Railway's initial evidence is that the attacker had 'abliterated' (safety-removed) AI models and substantial compute that enabled the exploits, which is a preliminary claim, not proven. The aim was stealing AI provider keys.

focus.title: testmetest npm worm arms 42 GitHub repos with AI coding-agent start-up hooks; wiper fires if you revoke the stolen token
focus.vendor: npm / GitHub (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code users)
focus.why: JFrog (Oct 26) found 42 legitimate GitHub repositories across 11 hijacked accounts carrying .claude/settings.json SessionStart hooks, .gemini/settings.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc and .vscode/tasks.json entries that launch a 13 MB disguised .github/init.js whenever someone opens the folder or starts an AI coding session. The linked npm worm (26 testmetest and @iobandamwer/* packages, run on install through binding.gyp with no install script) steals SSH, npm, PyPI, cloud, Kubernetes, browser and Claude/Codex/Gemini/Copilot credentials, republishes packages the victim can publish, and plants the same agent hooks in the victim's repos. Corgea and Rafter report a 'net-health-checker' service that checks the stolen GitHub token every 45 seconds for 48 hours and deletes the home folder if the token stops working. npm replaced the latest packages with security placeholders on Oct 26.
focus.action: Before opening a cloned repo in an AI coding agent or VS Code, check for unexpected .claude, .gemini, .cursor, .vscode/tasks.json, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or a large .github/init.js. Search lockfiles for *-testmetest and @iobandamwer/* packages. If a machine ran them, first disconnect it and stop and remove the net-health-checker and pkg-runtime services (~/.local/bin/net-health-checker.sh, ~/.local/share/runtimes/sync.py), then revoke GitHub, npm and cloud tokens and AI provider keys from a clean machine, and look for project-utils repos or 'AutoSyncComplete:' commits in your GitHub account.
focus.ai_note: The worm uses AI coding agents' own start-up hooks and rule files as the trigger, and steals AI assistant tokens alongside cloud keys.

focus.title: Adobe Commerce / Magento PolyShell CVE-2026-48356: exploited (CISA KEV), hundreds of stores breached with a hidden loader
focus.why: Moved up from the watch list (Oct 28): CISA added the unrestricted file-upload flaw (CVSS 9.3) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 27 (US federal deadline Nov 10). Sansec found 953 online stores, mostly Magento, injected since July 2025 with a scanner-evading JavaScript loader stored in CMS blocks; 471 were entered via PolyShell and others via SessionReaper CVE-2025-54236 or a rogue admin account. The loader fetches an attacker payload, but no next-stage malware has been recovered, so the goal (likely card skimming) is unconfirmed.
focus.action: Apply Adobe APSB26-73, then check cms_block and cms_page tables for unknown scripts (latest loader domain deepveindrilling[.]com), audit admin accounts, and rotate admin and payment-integration credentials if you find anything.

news.title: Discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities in critical, real-world software with Claude
news.blurb: An unreleased Claude model found critical flaws and wrote five full exploit chains, including a one-click Chrome sandbox escape; Chrome 156 fixes 62 resulting CVEs.

news.title: PHP2Shell Attack Roots 25 Servers, Breaches U.S. Government-Affiliated Network
news.blurb: Dream ties a China-linked, AI-assisted campaign (Claude Code, DeepSeek and Kimi tooling) to a custom PHP2Shell plus Fragnesia chain that rooted 25 servers and tunnelled into a US government-affiliated network.

news.title: Volt Typhoon hides zero-day attacks using 'Silent Train' framework
news.blurb: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs says Volt Typhoon built throwaway relay chains of hacked routers and used them for zero-days against VeloCloud Orchestrator, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, N-able N-central and Versa Director.

news.title: Opik Security Incident: October 2026
news.blurb: An attacker used an inactive user's API key and a flaw in Opik's AI provider settings to grab 29 of Comet's internal OpenAI and Anthropic keys; Comet says no customer data or keys were accessed and the keys are revoked.

news.title: n0n Ransomware: Inside an AI-Assisted Extortion Operation
news.blurb: An n0n operator used the opencode AI coding agent with 154 model entries to write hundreds of attack scripts; 93 victims listed.

news.title: CISA warns of hackers now exploiting critical Node2Shell flaw
news.blurb: The Brotli decoder RCE that OpenAI says its AI red-teaming found is in CISA KEV with a Nov 10 federal deadline.

news.title: CyberStrikeAI Uses 44 AI Agents to Automate Hacking Operations Against Japan Targets
news.blurb: Trend Micro's TrendAI documents an attacker platform splitting attacks across 44 AI agents, hitting at least 19 organizations.

news.title: Sony ISP subsidiary data breach exposes 2.5 million customer records
news.blurb: So-net's member database was accessed on Oct 19: 2.59 million records (names, phones, emails, birth dates, connection IDs) plus 54,401 email passwords, which Sony reset; NTT Docomo warns of follow-on phishing.

watch: Comet Opik (AI evaluation platform, Oct 24-26): an attacker used an inactive account's API key and a flaw in Opik's AI provider settings to obtain 29 of Comet's internal OpenAI and Anthropic keys; Comet says no customer data, accounts or keys were accessed, revoked the keys and now requires the key to be re-entered when a provider address changes. If you self-host Opik or store provider keys in similar tools, update, restrict provider endpoints and watch provider usage.

Sony Network Communications (So-net, Japan): attackers took 2,585,481 customer records on Oct 19 (names, phone numbers, emails, user IDs, birth dates, gender, connection IDs) and the passwords of 54,401 email accounts, which Sony reset on Oct 27; 443,495 of the records are NTT Docomo plala (S Course) customers. Expect phishing; affected users should set new passwords via So-net My Page.

Juniper Session Smart Router CVE-2026-103409 (9.8, published Oct 28): an unauthenticated attacker can get admin rights through an insecure root endpoint on devices not yet onboarded to Mist/Conductor; fixed in 7.0.5, 7.1.7 and 7.2.3 (bulletin JSA112183, no workaround). Session Smart Conductor CVE-2026-103406 (9.8, command injection via a crafted salt minion ID) is in the same batch. Juniper knows of no exploitation.

Volt Typhoon 'Silent Train' (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, Oct 28): China's Volt Typhoon has run throwaway relay chains of hacked SOHO routers, IoT and enterprise devices since late 2023 and used them for zero-days in VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-16812), Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN (CVE-2026-20127), N-able N-central (CVE-2025-8875, CVE-2025-8876) and Versa Director (CVE-2024-39717), plus a suspected Quest KACE zero-day. Patch those, keep management interfaces off the internet and keep longer log retention.

MLflow CVE-2026-116692 (CVSS 9.8, RCE) and CVE-2026-116690 (7.5, arbitrary file read): both work against default no-auth MLflow tracking servers; upgrade to MLflow 3.17.0 and put authentication in front of the server. A single X post claims CVE-2026-116690 is exploited, but GitHub's advisory, Feedly and TheHackerWire show no confirmed exploitation or KEV listing (unverified).

Fake AI desktop apps (Check Point via X, Oct 28, unverified here): GitHub Pages sites ranking in Google search offer 'GPT-6 Astra' and 'Claude Opus' desktop apps that bundle a real signed OpenAI or Claude installer with a crypto-miner; download AI apps only from the vendor's own site.

Langflow CVE-2026-105740: MCP stdio command injection lets any authenticated user run shell commands; ZoomEye counts about 19,200 exposed instances. Update Langflow and don't expose it to the internet (no attacks reported).
US Federal Election Commission took its electronic filing system offline on Oct 26 after an attempted breach (X report; details unconfirmed).

Unverified X claims: GFI Kerio Connect webmail stored XSS CVE-2026-112353 (fixed in 10.0.8 Patch 2) and the Bricksforge WordPress plugin upload flaw CVE-2026-85097 (fixed in 4.0.1) are being exploited; update both.

Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-101767 (CVSS 9.8, unauthenticated SQL injection leading to RCE in the TCF servlet /OA_HTML/AppsTCFServer, EBS 12.2.3-12.2.15, found by Horizon3.ai): Defused's decoys logged the first exploratory attempts on Oct 27, about a week after Oracle's Oct 20 Critical Patch Update fixed it; no confirmed intrusions yet. Apply the October CPU (MOS Note KA923); until then remove /OA_HTML/AppsTCFServer from the EBS URL firewall allowlist, restrict the web tier to trusted networks, and look for unauthenticated POSTs to that path invoking GanttDataServer and oracle-account shells from the Concurrent Manager.
Gotenberg CVE-2026-40281 (exploited ExifTool argument injection dropping a Go reverse shell): upgrade to 8.31.0+, keep it off the internet and check hosts running it (moved off the focus list).

Skyw4lker device-code phishing (ANY.RUN via The Hacker News, Oct 28): a campaign mostly against US organizations abuses Microsoft's device-code sign-in flow to take over corporate accounts without stealing passwords; block device-code flow with Conditional Access where it isn't needed.

Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 (9.8, in CISA KEV): ZDI says the zero-day ShinyHunters has exploited since May (mostly universities, then a wider September wave across tech, healthcare, government and more) is three chained flaws: an SSRF in the Integration Gateway reaches the Environment Management Hub because 127.0.0.1 is trusted by default, then a log-write command plants a web shell or an XMLDecoder file runs code on restart. Attackers bypassed WAF rules by requesting /%50SEMHUB/. Apply Oracle's June 10 security alert fix for PeopleTools 8.61/8.62, or disable/remove PSEMHUB; if exposed, hunt for web shells and rotate credentials reachable from the PeopleSoft tier, since patching doesn't evict an intruder.

Fortinet FortiSIEM CVE-2026-106173 (9.4, unauthenticated RCE via gRPC on TCP 27918, public PoC, exploitation reported by Canada's Cyber Centre, not yet in CISA KEV): upgrade 7.5.0 to 7.5.1+ or 7.6, block TCP 27918 from untrusted hosts and check cron-run scripts such as /opt/charting/redishb.sh (moved off the focus list).

llama.cpp CVE-2026-118375 (CVSS 9.2, published Oct 28): out-of-bounds stack write in the ggml-rpc RDMA transport lets an unauthenticated peer crash a llama.cpp rpc-server or possibly run code; builds b8841 up to b11865 are affected. Update to b11865 or later and never expose rpc-server to untrusted networks. No attacks reported.

Veeam Backup & Replication CVE-2026-108142 (CVSS 9.1, published Oct 27): unauthenticated authorization bypass in the CDP Coordinator Service on v13.0 and 13.1 (12.x not affected). No attacks reported, but Veeam servers are a favorite ransomware target; upgrade to 13.1.2.57 or 13.0.3.63 and restrict network access to the CDP Coordinator (Veeam KB4948).

NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit CVE-2026-65145 (CVSS 10.0, missing authentication, may allow code execution) affects 1.0 to 1.8.0; fixed in 1.9.0 (PyPI package nvidia-nat, released Sep 10). Also CVE-2026-65151 SQL injection fixed in 1.7.0. No attacks reported (NVIDIA bulletin 5912, Oct 27).

Aokigahara infostealer (Check Point, Oct 27): steals session and config files for Claude Code/Desktop, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT Desktop, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI, plus Git, SSH and cloud credentials. If a developer machine was infected, sign out of and revoke those AI tool sessions and rotate keys from a clean device.

EPICS Base (control software for particle accelerators and fusion experiments): Causal Security's autonomous agent Cipher found four flaws in under four hours, including critical CVE-2026-114595 (9.8, heap write, possible RCE); CISA advisory Oct 27; update to EPICS 7.0.11. No attacks reported.

Convertr: a card-skimming group reportedly compromised a shared analytics script used by the e-commerce platform to steal shoppers' card data at checkout (BleepingComputer, Oct 27). If your store loads Convertr scripts, check what they serve and watch for card fraud reports.

Cairn AI agents broke into websites of 100+ companies (Deere, SharkNinja, Cummins vendor), Reuters reports, using a mix of DeepSeek and Claude Code at about $50 per successful hack; patch e-commerce sites and admin panels and watch for web shells (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Fortinet patched critical flaws found by frontier AI testing in FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator, with details withheld until Nov 10; apply the October updates now (moved off the focus list; no new details).
RMS Cloud (holiday-park booking software) is reportedly investigating a breach; guests report fake emails, texts and WhatsApp messages (single X post, unverified).

Tailscale: v1.104.4 was published on GitHub at 01:05 UTC Oct 28 (9:05 PM EDT Oct 27), and Tailscale's security bulletins list fixes in 1.104.4 or newer, including Tailscale SSH memory exhaustion (TS-2026-015), Serve Unix backends reaching privileged sockets such as the tailscaled local API (TS-2026-016) and HTTP/2 capability mix-ups in Serve (TS-2026-017). The bulletins do not name 'Tailworm' or Cyberdione Labs, so whether all 11 Tailworm findings are covered is not confirmed. Update clients to 1.104.4 now; keep TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 and tight SSH rules until Tailscale confirms full coverage; headscale up to 0.29.6 was also listed as affected. No exploitation reported.

AI/MCP tool command-injection batch (published Oct 27, CVSS up to 8.5, no attacks reported): ai-sdlc plugin MCP server through 0.31.2 (CVE-2026-117558), DroidMind through 0.4.0 (CVE-2026-117559), ATXP Gemini CLI extension through 1.0.0 (CVE-2026-117560), sf-mcp through 1.3.2 (CVE-2026-117561), esp-mcp (CVE-2026-117567), mcp-ffmpeg through 1.0.5 (CVE-2026-117568), Kali-GPT (CVE-2026-117569) and hagent (CVE-2026-117573); also an unbounded request-size flaw in the official MCP TypeScript SDK HTTP transports (GHSA-f897-62hf-6gxq) and LiteLLM file read and XSS advisories (GHSA-g5ff-637f-6q2m, GHSA-hhww-mrg2-969h). Update or remove these tools.

Adobe Campaign Classic: several critical flaws published Oct 27, including SQL injection CVE-2026-105781 (CVSS 10.0) and code-execution bugs CVE-2026-105489, -105780, -104351 and -104353 (9.9); Adobe Connect CVE-2026-48360 (9.6) code injection. No attacks reported; apply Adobe's updates.

LiteLLM 1.107.0 backdoored on PyPI and Docker after a leaked AI-agent platform key (AI supply chain): If 1.107.0 (or the latest, main-latest or main-stable images on Oct 21) was installed, pulled or mirrored: don't run python or pip in that environment; investigate from a clean machine, delete cook.pth, cook.py and sitecustomize.py or better rebuild images and venvs, pin 1.106.2 by digest, and rotate every reachable credential from a clean machine (provider keys in the proxy DB, master and virtual keys, DATABASE_URL, cloud roles, CI, registry and Git tokens). Block litellm[.]dev. No CVE has been assigned. (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Bubble no-code platform breach: attacker took some users' API Connector and plugin credentials: If you build on Bubble: rotate every third-party API key or token stored in API Connector calls and plugins (payment, email, CRM, AI provider keys), check those services' usage logs since Oct 26, and set your app editor to 'Private app' unless it must be public. Plugin developers should rotate private keys stored in their plugins. Trust only messages from bubble.io and status.bubble.io. (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Treg (AI agent tools platform): an attacker ran commands on its production web service on Oct 23 via a server-side feature, apparently to steal AI inference provider keys, which treg ties to a series of attacks on platform companies. If you added your own keys (e.g. OpenRouter or other AI providers) to treg, rotate them at the provider and review October usage; all treg tokens were reset.

ENGIE (BleepingComputer, Oct 27): attackers took French customers' names, postal and email addresses, phone numbers, customer IDs, contract numbers and electricity PDL / gas PCE meter IDs from a tool partners use to sell energy offers; ENGIE says its internal systems and banking data were not affected and has not said how many customers. Expect phishing and fake 'ENGIE' calls that quote real contract details.

AfD (German party) hosting provider breach: Have I Been Pwned confirmed 345,000+ unique email addresses plus large volumes of emails and attachments taken from AfD-owned host Alternita in September (The Register, Oct 27). The attackers' claim that entry was via a poorly protected WordPress site is unverified.

DreamHost forced password resets for all email and FTP/SFTP users in a still-unexplained incident; if you host there, set new unique passwords, check mail forwarding rules and review site files changed since Oct 23 (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Gheist: stolen GitHub tokens used to plant secret-dumping 'ci-sync-*' workflow branches in 850+ accounts' repos; search for branches matching ci-sync-[0-9a-z]{6} and the 'gheist' user agent, and rotate secrets if found (moved off the focus list; no new details).

Denver Health Medical Plan: AI/ML analytics vendor SquareML left a live read-only database access key on a public website from Jun 27, 2025 to Aug 2026, exposing health data of 238,083 members to possible access; no evidence it was used (SecurityWeek, Oct 27).
Flowise CVE-2026-73487: its CSV and Airtable agents ran model-written Python after only a regex blocklist check, so a prompt could run code; fixed in Flowise 3.1.3. No attacks reported.

FortiBleed 2.0 (Infostealers.com, Oct 27): a newly obtained set of FortiGate configuration reports from around February 2026 holds 40,573 records with cleartext secrets, including 37,076 local-user and 1,576 Active Directory LDAP bind records, covering 975 domains not in the first leak. If you run FortiGate, rotate local VPN and LDAP bind passwords and check whether your domain is listed (single source).

SiteGuard Server Edition (Japanese web application firewall) CVE-2026-106931: OS command injection in the default-on statistics feature runs commands as root/SYSTEM; exploited and in CISA KEV (added Oct 20). Upgrade Apache/Nginx/IIS editions to Ver8.00 Update5 (FreeBSD to Ver7.00 Update6) per JPCERT, and preserve logs before patching.

Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX: Tanto Security published a RadImageEditor arbitrary file read that leaks web.config and can lead to RCE if the right secrets are there; update to 2026.3.812 and rotate machine keys if exposed. No attacks reported.

Lazarus 'Operation FlashHole' (Kaspersky via The Hacker News, Oct 27): North Korea-linked attackers abused South Korean security software to deploy malware using post-quantum encryption against at least three construction, software and telecom-equipment firms.
Amadey botnet: Australian authorities got into the malware's backend and cut off access to about 180,000 infected computers (The Hacker News, Oct 27).
Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 9.9, exploited, in CISA KEV): on-prem VCO upgrade to 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 or 6.4.2.12 and restrict web access (moved off the focus list).

Lightning AI Studio breach (since Oct 15): Studio, Deployments, Pipelines and Drive still offline; rotate every secret stored in a Studio and review connected services' logs (moved off the focus list).

Frontline Education (school administration software used by 80,000+ US schools) says attackers used a flaw in third-party software on Aug 14-15 to steal data from Frontline Central and School Health Management, now confirmed to include student data such as names, Social Security numbers, birth dates, government IDs and Medicaid or student IDs (Cybernews, Oct 27). Districts in several states are notifying families; expect phishing.

Dahua cameras in Ukraine: CERT-UA warns of unauthorised remote access to Dahua IP cameras and DVRs (video stream access, config changes, added accounts) via P2P cloud access and authentication weaknesses (The Hacker News, Oct 27). Update firmware, change default passwords, turn off P2P/Easy4IP and keep cameras off the internet.

UNM Health (New Mexico's largest hospital network) diverted ambulances and cancelled appointments and classes on Oct 26 because of a cybersecurity incident; operations began resuming in phases that afternoon and law enforcement is involved (UNM HSC, AP). Cause not disclosed.

University of Copenhagen (BleepingComputer, Oct 26): hackers reached a test environment holding names, national ID (CPR) numbers, phone numbers and emails of 525,000 people, plus PIN codes for 20,000 staff and students; expect targeted phishing if you are affected.

Apple CVE-2026-86950 (CoreGraphics zero-day that may have been exploited): Apple shipped extra patches including iOS and iPadOS 18.7.11 for older devices, per an X post from the ApplSec account; update older iPhones and iPads.

New critical CVEs, no attacks reported: Kener status page CVE-2026-116747 auth bypass (fixed in 4.1.10) and OpenPanel analytics CVE-2026-116818 unauthenticated ClickHouse SQL injection plus three more flaws (fixed in 3.0.0).

KB Kookmin Bank (Oct 26) says re-checking its earlier breach found 2,091 more people affected (1,631 customers, 460 staff), for 2,210 total; names, phone numbers, addresses and encrypted resident numbers leaked via a mobile staff work system.

Unverified X chatter (Oct 26): Electrum Bitcoin wallet 4.8.3 reportedly fixes a high-severity flaw that let malicious servers tamper with pending transactions after a theft; a researcher says he found remote code execution in the sandboxes of the Instinct and Muse personal-agent apps; and posts say a PS5 jailbreak (firmware 13.60-14.10, patched in 14.20) uses an AI-discovered hypervisor bug.
Nextcloud's built-in Collabora CODE Server app CVE-2026-110447 is exploited to plant web shells and is in CISA KEV; update richdocumentscode to 26.4.303 or later (moved off the focus list).

Genesys (contact-centre software) says attackers accessed its internal learning-management and CRM systems (announced Oct 19, contained Oct 23) and likely downloaded customer business contacts and account information; Genesys Cloud and Engage platforms and customer data in them were not affected. ScarlettGroup claimed the attack. Watch for phishing impersonating Genesys.

OVHcloud CLI release swap (Oct 19, 12:47-14:21 UTC): a hijacked contributor GitHub account replaced v0.11.0-v0.15.0 binaries with a stealer (about 250 downloads per StepSecurity) that took AWS, GCP, Azure, SSH, Kubernetes, npm and Terraform credentials plus Claude agent, Cursor, Continue, Cody and OpenCode data. If you installed or updated it in that window, look for envchecker-* folders in your temp directory, move to v0.16.0 and rotate everything on that machine (advisory GHSA-862f-55f5-vmvw).

OpenHands Software Agent SDK CVE-2026-112346 (9.8, published Oct 26): Docker and Apptainer workspace launchers bound the agent server to all interfaces with authentication off by default, so anyone who reaches the port can run code; upgrade to 1.52.0 and don't expose sandbox ports. No attacks reported.

Xint 'compaction smuggling' (SecurityWeek, Oct 26): a flaw in OpenAI's context-compaction API let researchers move hidden reasoning traces to another model and read them, which could aid distillation of frontier models; OpenAI fixed it and paid a bounty on Oct 23. Nothing for users to do.
OpenCode Console breach (Oct 22): saved OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API keys were exposed; if you stored provider keys there, rotate them and check provider usage logs (moved off the focus list).

Mirae Asset Life Insurance (South Korea) confirmed on Oct 26 that customer personal credit information leaked after intruders reached parts of its subscription system and website (detected Oct 25); the exact data and number of customers are still being identified and the website is blocked (SBS/Yonhap). Expect phishing aimed at its customers.

Microsoft Authenticator for Android CVE-2026-80097 ('AuthMask', CVSS 8.6): a malicious app with no permissions could impersonate Teams and get mail, files and calendar tokens for the signed-in work account (Enclave, Oct 23). Patched Sep 8 in 6.2606.4246; no attacks reported. Make sure managed Android devices run 6.2606.4246 or later.

Blastmail (Japanese email newsletter service run by Rakus Light Cloud): down since Oct 21 after an intruder ran commands on two API servers and took data on all contract holders, plus subscriber lists for 345 contracts (Oct 26 update; next report Oct 27 noon JST). Expect targeted phishing to Blastmail customers and their newsletter subscribers.

Linux kernel ZDI-CAN-33367 (skb_zerocopy, CVSS 7.8): public proof-of-concept gives an unprivileged local user root on Debian 12/13, Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 and AlmaLinux 8-10 even with the Dirty Frag fix; no CVE, no in-the-wild use reported. AlmaLinux has patched kernels in testing (4.18.0-553.177.2.el8_10, 5.14.0-687.59.2.el9_8, 6.12.0-211.68.2.el10_2); until your distro ships a fix, set user.max_user_namespaces=0 or block the esp4/esp6 modules on multi-user hosts and container nodes (AlmaLinux, Sysdig).

AdFection (Citizen Lab, Oct 15): Israeli ad-tech firm Discover-Tech allegedly used targeted online ads to profile devices and deliver zero-click Candiru spyware (confirmed infections at Al Jazeera). ABC Australia says ads from the network reached a small number of staff devices, found no signs of compromise and is wiping them as a precaution (Oct 23); more than two dozen Australian government, critical-infrastructure and university targets are named as a cluster. Use ad blocking on sensitive devices.

Fireworks AI (inference and fine-tuning platform): internal credentials were misused Oct 6 to read environment variables in evaluation jobs for a limited number of customer accounts; affected customers were notified. If you got a notice, replace the revoked Fireworks keys and rotate the third-party credentials it lists at their issuing providers.
Unverified X chatter: a dark-web post advertises about 207,857 customer account and order records from Taiwanese marketplace Popchill.

npm (Oct 25) replaced 19 packages from the appit-online publisher account with security placeholders; insta-api-wrapper and ionic-insta-api-wrapper sent Instagram usernames, passwords and session tokens to reelsaver.appit-online[.]de and used them to auto-follow and like. If you used any appit-online package, remove it and reset affected Instagram sessions (Corgea write-up).

Zeabur hosting platform: attackers read 3.2 million environment-variable records (Oct 14-15) and Zeabur is shutting down (shared clusters pause Dec 1, everything stops Dec 31). If you stored secrets there, revoke them at the issuing provider, rebuild dedicated servers and migrate (moved off the focus list; see Zeabur's incident report).

New AI-infrastructure CVEs (no attacks reported): vLLM CVE-2026-116176 (SSRF, fixed in 0.24.0) and CVE-2026-116177/116179/116180 (memory and denial-of-service issues, fixed by 0.25.0 to 0.31.0), so run vLLM 0.31.0+; AWS Labs postgres-mcp-server CVE-2026-85787 (SQL validation gap lets read-only callers modify data) and mysql-mcp-server CVE-2026-85788, so update those MCP servers. LiteLLM's MCP auth bypass CVE-2026-59822 (fixed in 1.84.0) has been in CISA KEV since Sep 2.

MCP Inspector (official Model Context Protocol debugging tool): two CVSS 9.6 flaws published Oct 21 (GHSA-4fc4-wcmh-4g86, GHSA-6x67-4w4w-9f3w) let a malicious remote MCP server run commands on your machine just by connecting or viewing its MCP App, plus a Windows/WSL OAuth-URL injection in 2.x; update to 1.0.3 (1.x) or 2.12.0 (2.x) and remove older pinned copies. No attacks reported.

AI coding agents and instruction files: don't start Codex, Claude Code, Cursor CLI or similar agents in ~/Downloads or your home folder, since any web page can drop an AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md there; review unfamiliar instruction files and keep approval prompts and sandboxing on (Forever Security via BleepingComputer, Oct 25).

SECRA Bookings (HomeToGo's holiday-rental channel-management unit): found an intrusion on Oct 23 in which attackers exported guest and partner data, possibly including bank details (IBANs), ID numbers and key-safe codes (HomeToGo ad-hoc statement, Oct 24). Hosts should reset door PINs and key-safe codes and treat SECRA integration keys and passwords as compromised.

MythicRatatoskr: ESET (Oct 25 via r/blueteamsec) describes a new Yggdrasil-enabled backdoor deployed jointly by UAC-0099 and Sandworm, Russia-linked groups that target Ukraine; see ESET's report for indicators.

and ST HD (Japanese apparel retailer, formerly Adastria): unauthorized access to its operational servers may have exposed about 2.5 million customer records, about 10,000 business-partner records and employee data (IR notice, Oct 23); card data is not affected and member-point use was paused. Expect phishing.

Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257 (auth bypass, in CISA KEV since May): Unit 42 (Oct 19-20 update) says Qilin and Inc ransomware operators are using it to get a VPN session past MFA, then move to vCenter/ESXi and domain controllers. Upgrade per Palo Alto's advisory or disable authentication-override cookies, or use a dedicated certificate for them.

eMudhra certificate authority CVE-2026-111943/111944: eight intermediate CA keys are trivially recoverable and now public; Mozilla, Google and Apple are distrusting them and Cisco published a notice, and Microsoft released out-of-band Windows updates (Oct 27) that distrust them for systems without automatic certificate trust updates. Update OS and app CA bundles and replace any certificates issued by eMudhra (moved off the focus list).

Unitree Go2 robot dog CVE-2026-115995 (9.6): command injection in the GPT voice-chat component (chat_go/gpt_thread.py) lets a remote attacker run OS commands; upgrade firmware to 1.1.11.5. No attacks reported.

Amadeus (airline booking and ticketing provider): Korean Air and Asiana say Amadeus told them on Oct 20 that customer reservation data, including booking references, was accessed with stolen Amadeus account credentials sometime between Aug 2023 and Sep 2026; payment data was not affected. heise separately reported (Oct 13) an Amadeus heap-dump flaw that exposed passport and booking data until it was fixed. Expect airline-themed phishing; other carriers may follow.

Keystone Hardware Wallet: update (Oct 26) the Oct 20 website intrusion, via a flaw in a third-party monitoring tool, also took the WebAuth key that proves devices are genuine, so counterfeit wallets could pass its authenticity check. Keystone is destroying 18,835 unsold devices and pausing shipments; devices delivered before Oct 20 that pass the check are fine, but anything received after Oct 20 needs extra verification through Keystone support before use. Recovery phrases and private keys were not exposed. Keystone will not ask for devices back, so treat any 'recall' request as a scam (Cointelegraph).
Pillow (Python imaging) CVE-2026-112900/112393/112403: critical flaws, one found by Claude; upgrade to Pillow 13.0.0 and rebuild images (moved off the focus list; no attacks reported).
Plex2Shell: Plex Media Server exploit chain CVE-2026-96652/96654/96655/96656 is in CISA KEV; update Plex Media Server per Plex's advisory (moved off the focus list).
Wasmtime CVE-2026-115889 (9.9, Cranelift miscompilation): update per GHSA-897f-g5gm-fmxm if you run untrusted WebAssembly; no attacks reported.
GitLab CVE-2026-110264 (CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE, self-managed): no attacks reported yet; upgrade to 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10 or 18.11.13 (moved off the focus list).
HPE Aruba AOS-8/AOS-10: eight CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated flaws (CVE-2026-79844 to -79851), no exploitation known; upgrade per HPESBNW05162 (moved off the focus list).

AhsayCBS backup servers CVE-2026-105133/105134: exploited since Oct 7 to drop web shells and miners at MSPs; earlier patches were incomplete, so apply hotfix 10.3.4.45 (v10) or 9.15.2.70 (v7-v9), reboot and check for compromise.

SafePay ransomware: CISA, FBI, USSS and UK/German partners (advisory AA26-293A, Oct 20) say about 600 victims, with entry via stolen VPN credentials and known edge-device flaws (Cisco ASA, Veeam, SonicWall CVEs listed); patch those, require MFA and keep offline backups.

Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (CVSS 9.5, exploited as zero-days, patched Sep 27 in 14.1-73.37 / 13.1-64.23): new write-ups show attackers left web shells, rogue accounts and SUID shells that survive patching; hunt with the published IOCs if you patched late.

GMO Internet's Onamae.com Desktop Cloud: an unauthorised program on customer servers (up to 26,739 servers) led to stolen trading-account logins and unauthorised trades; all servers suspended. Users should change trading credentials from another device and enable 2FA. GMO says the attacker has demanded money; it refused and went to police. An unverified statement attributed to the attacker demands US$1 million by noon JST Oct 27 (11 PM EDT Oct 26) and threatens more trading-account abuse and leaks (BreachNews, Oct 25). Update (Oct 26): Euronews reports GMO will compensate affected users; a Japanese blog citing GMO's fifth report says the demand rose to US$50 million (unverified). Update (Oct 27, GMO's 8th notice): the attacker threatened to publish customer data and launch ransomware at noon JST Oct 27 (11 PM EDT Oct 26); GMO told users to back up, run a full antivirus scan, disconnect and power off their PCs before then, is analysing collected customer PCs with Trend Micro's help, and again refused to pay. No outcome reported yet. Update (Oct 27, per GMO's notices as summarised by TrustList; not independently verified): GMO confirms customer information was taken and some customers saw trades they did not make; it will pay every current customer 5,000 yen, offer six months free on a replacement service and cover realised losses from unauthorised trades, with details by email before 23:59 JST Oct 30. Whether the threatened noon leak and ransomware attack happened is not yet reported. Update (Oct 27, NHK): after GMO ignored the noon JST deadline, the group released what it claims is customer information and threatens daily releases at noon; GMO says it will not pay and is working with police. Authenticity of the leaked data is not confirmed. Update (GMO's 10th report, Oct 27 13:55 JST): GMO confirmed the attackers published what they claim is company and customer data at 12:30 JST, warns that visiting the leak site exposes visitors' information to the attackers, and says no ransomware attack had been confirmed; it will contact customers individually if their data is in the leak. Update (Oct 28, GMO's 13th report and BleepingComputer): no ransomware was activated on customer machines and GMO's analysis of submitted PCs had found no malware as of Oct 27; the attackers' leak site and mirrors were taken down around 4 AM JST Oct 28 (3 PM EDT Oct 27). GMO says the original demand was about 8 billion yen (about $50 million), will not pay, and warns it may take legal action against anyone who spreads the leaked data. Update (Oct 28, The Hacker News): GMO opened a 'GMO Cybercrime Bounty' of up to $1 million total for tips leading to an arrest or international wanted notice (open until Oct 27, 2027); OANDA Japan confirmed a third party traded on some customers' accounts with ID/password pairs it believes leaked from the GMO servers, and FXTF told Desktop Cloud users to change passwords from a device that never connected to it. GMO still hasn't said how the attackers got in; they claim one admin account was shared across all servers (unconfirmed). Update (Oct 28, IBTimes via r/cybersecurity): purported customer data keeps appearing online after GMO refused to pay; authenticity still unconfirmed.

Quest Diagnostics confirmed (8-K, Oct 23) that attackers accessed patient records via its Quanum lab system; Capcom says 11.77 million CAPCOM ID email addresses were stolen. Alliance Medinet (Singapore healthcare administrator for HSBC Life, Great Eastern and Income Insurance) says about 110,000 members' names, ID numbers and contact details were taken from its membership database (Oct 24 filing).
Ray (AI compute engine) CVE-2025-62593, browser-based RCE in CISA KEV: upgrade to Ray 2.52.0+.

AI developer tools patched this week: Aider CVE-2026-115726 (malicious repo .aider.conf.yml runs commands, through 0.86.2), Hugging Face Datasets CVE-2026-57845 (pickle RCE, through 5.1.0), Azure AI Foundry CVE-2026-108456 (SSRF privilege escalation), plus vLLM CVE-2026-114053 (fixed in 0.31.0) and LiteLLM CVE-2026-114612 (per X).
Linux KSMBD: two CVSS 9.0 RCE flaws with no mainline fix yet; disable ksmbd if you don't need in-kernel SMB.

PingCAP/TiDB confirmed (CEO note, Oct 23) that an attacker used a compromised GitHub account and exposed credentials from Sep 9 to Oct 7 to copy source code and customer-related data; TiDB Cloud API-key values were encrypted, but credentials shared in support materials were not. Replace TiDB Cloud management API keys and rotate anything shared with PingCAP support. FulcrumSec claims (unverified, via InfoQ Oct 25) 115,000 console API keypairs (40,000+ active) and about 1,800 customer database endpoints with root or admin logins from migration jobs; if you ran a TiDB Cloud migration, rotate the source database credentials too. Update (InfoQ, Oct 25): the extortion group FulcrumSec claims 10.6 TB including 115K console API keypairs (40K+ active) and about 1,800 customer database endpoints with admin accounts; unverified, but rotate TiDB Cloud API keys and any database credentials used in migration jobs.

Swell swETH/rswETH: compromised oracle hot keys inflated token rates and four malicious upgrade contracts were staged (about 2,500 ETH at risk, not a confirmed loss); deposits and withdrawals are paused. The Railway link is unconfirmed.

Also new and patched: PwnEscape CVE-2026-99999 (KVM guest-to-host, AlmaLinux 8-10 affected), Laravel TokenGuard auth bypass (fixed in 12.68.0 / 13.29.0), OpenWrt odhcpd CVE-2026-53921 (9.8, public PoC).
PwC confirmed a cybersecurity incident at a third-party vendor hosting employee learning records after Everest claimed 590 GB of data; PwC did not verify the claimed size or contents.

Navigate360 (school and police anonymous tip platform) confirmed attackers took about 8.3 million tip records between Nov 2025 and Mar 2026, which may include student names, birth dates and Social Security numbers; Nevada's SafeVoice is affected and other states' schools too.

Sagawa Express says up to 53.23 million sets of shipping-label personal data may have been exposed via its tracking service (Jun 21 to Sep 30); Park24 confirmed about 1.46 million encrypted ID-document images were sent out of its Times Car systems and will pay 3,000 yen per affected user.

Microsoft 365 token spraying: Huntress tracked an attacker replaying post-MFA session tokens (from AiTM phishing and device-code phishing) from 193.26.115.0/24 into 79 organizations (Jul-Sep), adding rogue Entra devices, MFA methods and hidden inbox rules. Enforce Conditional Access for all users and apps; on compromise revoke sessions and remove attacker devices and MFA methods, not just reset the password.
BlackX UEFI bootkit (Kaspersky, attributed to APT41) bypasses Secure Boot on patched Windows systems that lack the boot-manager revocations; apply Microsoft's Secure Boot DBX/revocation updates.

Treasure Factory (Japanese resale chain) says an intruder exploited its home buy-back booking system on Oct 20 and took 746,277 customer email addresses; it says the PHP flaws were not the cause. Expect phishing.

PK Softech, a software provider to Swiss pension funds (including Publica, BPK and BLVK), had data stolen in a cyberattack; Switzerland's data protection commissioner opened a formal investigation on Oct 23.

Unverified X chatter: a P3 tip-platform breach exposing 1.5M+ Canadian Crime Stoppers tips; ~$371k of crypto reportedly drained from wallets whose keys were stored on Railway; seller 'ls1337' offering an alleged Mistral AI trade-secrets dataset for $30,000; Good Smile Company store-admin intrusion (Oct 19-22); Qilin claiming Commonwealth Community Bank; GMO Desktop Cloud attackers now demanding money; an X user says 35,000 profiles on the Maxed AI app were wiped via mass delete requests.

Lotte Giftiel (South Korean mobile-coupon service run by Spoon): an intruder on Oct 22 took 18,359 customers' names, phone numbers, emails and bank account numbers; no fraudulent coupon use confirmed. Expect phishing.

ai_activity.overview: In the last 7 days AI has shown up on every side of attacks. New on Oct 28: Comet disclosed that an attacker pulled 29 internal OpenAI and Anthropic keys through a flaw in Opik's AI provider settings, and honeypot data shows 175 IPs sending working PHP2Shell payloads; also on Oct 28, the first documented real intrusion using AI-found PHP2Shell was itself AI-assisted (Claude Code and DeepSeek/Kimi tooling, 25 servers rooted, a US government-affiliated network reached), SOCRadar showed the n0n extortion crew used an AI coding agent to write hundreds of attack scripts, and fake GPT-6 and Claude installers and an MLflow RCE (exploitation unverified) put AI users and ML servers at risk. New on Oct 27: Anthropic's red team showed an unreleased Claude model writing a one-click Chrome sandbox escape (62 Chrome CVEs fixed in Chrome 156), and Causal Security's Cipher agent found four EPICS flaws in under four hours. AI agents also ran large campaigns (CyberStrikeAI's 44 agents, Storm-0940's ARTEX at ConnectWise, Cathedral at Anthropic, Warp), while breaches at Railway, treg, Comet Opik, OpenCode and LiteLLM went after AI provider keys.

items.title: PHP2Shell: PHP RCE found with AI, now used in an AI-assisted real intrusion (25 servers rooted, US government-affiliated network reached)
items.summary: New (Oct 28): The Hacker News reports Dream found Claude Code on the attacker's infrastructure plus an AI offensive platform (aiscan) running DeepSeek and Kimi models and about 40 AI-styled scripts, in a China-linked campaign that rooted 25 servers, mostly one vendor's firewalls, with a custom PHP2Shell plus Fragnesia chain. New (Oct 26): CISA added both CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. New (Oct 26): Perplexity's Adel Karimi confirmed 35 successful shells on PHP 8.4.26 honeypots (Oct 24), backed by Expel's Marcus Hutchins (BleepingComputer); Delft's tracker counts 171 IPs sending exploit code. Calif found the flaws first partly with frontier AI; Wiz (Atlas agent) and OpenAI's Codex Security found them independently. On Oct 25 Unit 42 retracted its Oct 23 report that an agentic AI attack platform used PHP2Shell to break into a European government agency: it still saw the AI-driven activity in a vulnerable PHP application but cannot confirm PHP2Shell was the entry point. Amazon sees broad exploitation attempts and Cloudflare millions of attempts; the PHP Foundation and Dataminr report no confirmed compromises of their own, and CrowdStrike expects weaponising obstacles to limit mass exploitation. CVE-2026-115560 is not fixed by the Oct 21 releases. Unverified X claim (Oct 25): the XHack AI agent wrote a working Python exploit against PHP 8.4.26 in a lab. Servers stay exposed until running PHP workers are restarted after patching. CISA publicly confirmed exploitation on Oct 27. New (Oct 27): Wiz says its telemetry shows about 67% fewer exposed vulnerable machines and that the attempts it has seen have not succeeded; CISA's federal patch deadline is Oct 29. Update (Oct 27): Palo Alto now confirms exploitation against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces. Update (Oct 28): ELLIO saw the same IP exploiting PHP2Shell also firing the public Brotli Node2Shell exploit. Update (Oct 28): Dream (via SecurityWeek) documents a China-linked actor chaining PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia kernel flaw (CVE-2026-46300) using an automated tool to root 24 firewalls on Oct 23-24 and reach a US government-affiliated organization's firewall management server.

items.title: Brotli decoder RCE (CVE-2026-111497, 'Node2Shell'): OpenAI says its AI red-teaming found it (credit disputed); now in CISA KEV
items.summary: OpenAI said on X that a red-team exercise found unauthenticated RCE in Brotli, bundled in Node.js, Bun and Envoy; the root cause was fixed upstream in February without being flagged as a vulnerability. Fixes shipped Oct 21; Imperva showed working RCE on an official Node.js build; no in-the-wild attacks reported. The Hacker News (Oct 24) confirms Bun, Python brotli/brotlicffi and Envoy are affected. Update Oct 25: ELLIO reproduced code execution on official x86-64 Node.js builds and saw a public scanner mapping Brotli-decoding hosts; no confirmed attacks yet. Update Oct 26: Microsoft shipped emergency .NET 8/9/10 fixes and public PoCs are on GitHub; BleepingComputer credits Imperva's Red Team with the discovery, so the AI-found claim rests on OpenAI's own post. Update (Oct 27): CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Update (Oct 28): BleepingComputer and SecurityWeek report CISA's exploitation confirmation (federal deadline Nov 10); ELLIO saw the public exploit fired from an IP that also exploits PHP2Shell.

items.title: SOCRadar: n0n extortion operator used the opencode AI coding agent (154 models, $7,216+ in LLM spend) to build hundreds of attack scripts; 93 victims listed
items.summary: An exposed staging server showed an AI coding agent, including safety-stripped models, writing and debugging breach, exfiltration, wiper and extortion scripts. Entry was all stolen or weak credentials (305 FortiGate SSL-VPNs credential-stuffed, exposed AWS keys, RDP/WinRM); 23 organizations in 14 countries are in the workspace, and n0n listed 93 victims and $283.7M in demands by Oct 19. Human-directed with AI support, not autonomous.

items.title: Anthropic Frontier Red Team: unreleased Claude model found critical flaws and built five full exploit chains, including a one-click Chrome sandbox escape
items.summary: The model found and exploited bugs in widely used browsers and operating systems; Google assigned and fixed 62 critical/high Chrome CVEs from the work in Chrome 156 (13 sandbox escapes). Chrome 156 also credits OpenAI Codex Security for one bug. No in-the-wild use reported.

items.title: Causal Security's Cipher agent found four EPICS Base flaws (one critical) in under four hours
items.summary: Autonomous agent found and validated CVE-2026-114595 (9.8) and CVE-2026-114596/114597/114598 in the control-system toolkit used at accelerators and fusion labs; CISA advisory; fixed in EPICS 7.0.11.

items.title: TrendAI: CyberStrikeAI ran 44 AI agents against at least 19 organizations (16 in Japan); two more AI-assisted operators found
items.summary: Trend Micro's TrendAI analysed three exposed attacker servers: one used the open-source CyberStrikeAI tool to automate the full attack chain with 44 agents and Japanese-language phishing pages in October; a second, LLM-assisted campaign targeted AI workflow platforms and inference services for cheap compute and stole data from a GIS server with default credentials; a third used AI to build tools for edge-device and WebLogic campaigns (Jan-Oct). No shared operator found.

items.title: Unit 42 and others: BUGSTER's Hermes/DeepSeek/Cursor attacks, a 10-hour mostly autonomous enterprise breach, Zerofot key harvesting with Codex and Claude Code, RAGE framework
items.summary: Round-up in The Hacker News: actor BUGSTER ran the Hermes agent framework on DeepSeek V4 with Cursor (safety controls off) against Indian universities and took 5,200+ student records; a human operator used frontier models to breach an enterprise network in 10 hours and turn its AI endpoints into attack infrastructure (Unit 42); a Gentlemen ransomware affiliate used Claude Code in six intrusions in late June; Zerofot's 'auto_scan' used OpenAI Codex and Claude Code to harvest thousands of API keys from exposed hosts; an AI-generated 'RAGE' framework exploits exposed Redis, Docker, Jenkins and similar services to drop miners. Exact dates of several cases are not given.
items.source: Unit 42 / Straiker / Hunt.io via The Hacker News

items.title: Warp: AI 'agent swarm' exploited a vendor in Warp's infrastructure and read agent trace and telemetry data
items.summary: Warp CEO Zach Lloyd said (Oct 26) that on Oct 23 Warp found an active, narrow exploitation of a third-party vendor, apparently by an agent swarm using a sophisticated penetration and escalation technique likely starting with a hole in a vendor dependency. It reached limited agent trace and telemetry data for up to about 1% of users; Warp remediated within hours and is investigating with CrowdStrike and law enforcement. The AI attribution is Warp's own assessment; the vendor and flaw are not named.

items.title: Seoul police: ex-pentester-led ring used the ARTEX AI pentest framework to hack 90+ organizations and steal 8.2 million records
items.summary: Seven suspects allegedly stole 8.2 million pieces of personal data and internal records from 90+ hospitals, private academies and businesses since September 2025, using AI tools to hack 60 of them; 38 suffered losses and were asked for a combined 360 million won (about $272,000). The 32-year-old ringleader, a former mock-hacking employee at a security company, has been referred to prosecutors (Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency via Yonhap). Update Oct 26: Seoul Economic Daily and SBS report the ringleader first ran web scanners by hand, then used an AI coding agent and an autonomous AI penetration-testing system to breach 60 companies in just over 40 days (Aug 31 to Oct 13); police say it is the same AI tool used in a recent South Korean financial-sector breach, though no link between the cases is confirmed. One victim paid 300,000 won. Update Oct 26 (BleepingComputer citing Yonhap): police say the 32-year-old leader, who worked at a security company in 2019-2022, switched from conventional tools to AI in late August 2026 and used the ARTEX AI penetration-testing suite, the same autonomous framework tied to attacks on South Korean banks, in most of the attacks; he was arrested Oct 15 and referred to prosecutors Oct 23, while six others are under investigation without detention. Police are checking whether the data was leaked on the dark web.

items.title: Unverified: PS5 jailbreak said to use an AI-discovered hypervisor bug
